subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which formula is used to calculate the mass of solute needed for a Molar solution?
questions.explain: $Mass = M \times V \times MW$. Molarity is moles/liter, so multiplying by Liters gives moles. Multiplying moles by g/mol gives grams.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: How many grams of NaCl (Molecular Weight = 58.44 g/mol) are required to prepare 500 mL of a 0.5 M solution?
questions.explain:
1. Convert Volume to L: 500 mL = 0.5 L. 
2. Calculate moles: $0.5 \text{ mol/L} \times 0.5 \text{ L} = 0.25 \text{ mol}$. 
3. Calculate mass: $0.25 \text{ mol} \times 58.44 \text{ g/mol} = 14.61 \text{ g}$.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which piece of glassware is most accurate for measuring the final volume of a solution?
questions.explain: A volumetric flask is calibrated to contain a precise volume at a specific temperature, making it the most accurate for preparing solutions.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 25°C?
questions.explain: pH 7 is neutral. <7 is acidic, >7 is basic.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: To adjust the pH of a buffer from 8.0 down to 7.4, which substance would you typically add?
questions.explain: To lower the pH (make it more acidic), you add an acid like HCl. Adding a base (NaOH) would raise the pH.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which of the following best defines a 'buffer'?
options: A solution that changes color when pH changes.
A solution that resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added.
A solution used to sterilize equipment.
questions.explain: Buffers are solutions containing a weak acid and its conjugate base that resist changes in pH.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: When using a pH meter, what is the first step before measuring your sample?
options: Calibrate the meter using standard buffers (e.g., pH 4, 7, 10).
Dry the electrode completely with a paper towel.
questions.explain: Calibration ensures accuracy. Electrodes drift over time and must be calibrated with standards of known pH.
